thread:
Anya: noticing a KV cache blowup on prod-us-east starting ~10m ago. continuous-batching queue keeps growing, paging events spiking. short requests (<=32 tokens) tail p50->p99 jump from 40ms to 1.8s
Mike: seeing same in traces, batch-scheduler showing starvation for short shapes when mixed with long shapes. pack sizes cluster at 512 repeatedly.
Priya: Paging alarms: pcb-paging-rate > 5x baseline, eviction pressure high. KV cache size increased 3x in last 8 minutes.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: kv-cache-continuous-batch-regression (sev-2) — oncall: mike — link: https://ops/incident/1718501234
Anya: customers A, B, C on dedicated pools reported elevated latencies in support tickets. CS flagged 2 P1s. @cs-elaine can you confirm?
Cs-elaine: confirmed — two enterprise customers (acct-327, acct-441) reported timeouts; I've opened support threads and started outbound. No escalations yet but they're getting slow.
Sean: hypothesis: prefetch loop + aggressive continuous batching window causing repeated packing of long and short requests, kv entries not being compacted, causing paging. Also see more cache misses during evictions leading to downstream cold loads.
Priya: mitigation options: 1) temporarily reduce continuous_batch_window from 100ms -> 20ms 2) turn off aggressive prefetch for tier=standard 3) emergency eviction throttle to cap KV growth. Which to try first?
Mike: I'd prefer reducing batch window first (low blast) -> reduces pack mixing. If quick and effective, we can then enable staged rollback.
Anya: agree. I'll push a config hotpatch to prod-us-east config map and rollout to the packer service canary.
Mike: patch snippet being applied:
```bash
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/packer CONT_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=20 --record
# then curl /admin/reload-config to pick up
```
Priya: also queue up a temporary route to redirect long-shape traffic to dedicated long-shape pool to avoid interference. That takes longer.
Infra-bot: deploy started for deployment/packer -> rollout id r-1718501240, canary 5% -> 50% expected in 4m.
Anya: monitoring key metrics: packer_pack_size, packer_queue_length, kv_cache_size_bytes, paging_rate, short_p99_latency. I'll post updates.
(2m later)
Anya: canary looks good at 5%: pack_size median down from 512 -> 96, queue length dropping. short_p99 improved from 1.9s -> 220ms.
Mike: good. continue rollout to 50%. keep an eye on paging_rate.
(4m later)
Anya: rollout to 50% done. paging_rate trending down, eviction rate stabilizing. no new timeouts reported in the 2 affected customer threads.
Cs-elaine: I've informed accounts A and B that we're rolling a fix, offered temporary credits and asked them to validate. They've acknowledged.
Mike: next: schedule a follow-up to revert any aggressive config toggles and implement a safer default: cont_batch_window should auto-tune by request-mix, not fixed. Add a guard to disable prefetch when cache pressure > 70%.
Priya: creating a short-lived hotfix PR to add prefetch disable flag and a metric-gated switch. PR: https://git/repo/pull/4482
Ops-lead: good job. Now decide whether to keep lower window permanently. We should let telemetry run for 1h, then either keep or backfill improvements. Also attach a rollback plan in case of regression.
Anya: telemetry for 30m shows sustained improvement: kv_cache_size down ~40% vs peak, paging_rate down 6x, short_p99 stable ~180-240ms. No new paging-induced errors.
Mike: I'll create an incident handoff note and assign postmortem: owner=priya, sla impact=no-data-loss, customer-impact=latency/timeouts for several sessions during peak window.
Oncall-bot: HANDOFF: mike -> night-oncall (sean). Details: patch rolled 1718501240, keep watch on packer queue and paging alarms, if paging_rate > 2x baseline for 10m, revert cont_batch_window to previous and disable prefetch.
Sean: taking handoff, will monitor dashboards and alerts. If anything spikes, will run rollback command:
```bash
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/packer CONT_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=100 && kubectl rollout restart deployment/packer
```
Anya: created incident thread in ops tracker and attached top graphs. Postmortem tasks assigned in the tracker.
Priya: notes for postmortem: root cause probable interplay between new continuous batching heuristics and prefetch heuristics — amplifies mixed-shape starvation leading to packing blowups and eviction cascades. Action items: adaptive batching, prefetch guard, improved packer fairness logic, chaos test for mixed-shape workloads.
Cs-elaine: I'll follow up with customers tomorrow with a summary and timelines for permanent fix.
Ops-lead: closing active mitigation. Severity downgrade to sev-3. Handoff to night-oncall Sean. Postmortem owner: priya. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
